profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21711 Filigree Court, Suite C, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC1 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC1 is a 19,935-square-foot building in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's multi-facility campus in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. The operator publishes no power capacity for this building specifically, though it describes 2N power redundancy, N+1 generator redundancy rated for 30+ hours at full load, and N+2 cooling redundancy. Without a published megawatt figure, the facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from specifications alone.

The Ashburn campus itself sits in the region described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, anchored by Equinix's own DC1 and DC2 buildings established in the late 1990s and expanded into numbered facilities into the twenties. Data Center Dynamics has called DC2 reputedly the most connected building on earth, and the campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia as a state ranks 24th by published megawatt capacity among all mapped data center sites, with 1,375.4 MW disclosed across 23 facilities out of 326 mapped in the state.

This building's power capacity remains unpublished, placing it outside the 23 Virginia facilities with disclosed specifications. The research note confirms that only DC2's specs are publicly detailed as a campus representative; determining whether DC1 has undergone capacity upgrades relevant to current AI demand would require direct re-fetching of the operator's current page for this facility.
